full_established_role_reported_before: Role: hydrolyzes arginine to urea and ornithine, the last step of the urea cycle, which runs mainly in the liver [@new:UniProt2025; @old:28]. Reported before [@new:Yuan2023ARG1; @new:FawadAliShah2018]; the earlier MR study's T2D data include those of our DIAMANTE check. The instrument of a published arginine–T2D MR, rs2246012, strongly tags the specified signal-A lead rs2781668 (r² 0.993 with A and 0.0020 with B on the 503 panel; same category on the 489 panel) [@old:24]. This is strong tagging of the specified lead, not proof of an identical causal signal or mediation pathway; the r² confirms a value recorded before this comparison, and the published result and our signal-A findings rest on substantially overlapping genetic evidence. Signal B's arginine and ornithine associations were reported before ([@old:24], Supplementary Table 5). Tractable, no agent with an ARG1 mechanism
full_adds: PP.H4 0.925 (0.553 conservative); with arginine 0.996. External check, DIAMANTE: OR 0.89 (0.81 to 0.98), p = 0.015; concordant, not Bonferroni; corroborated, confirmatory; ARG1 was chosen as the principal worked example after the pre-stated rule returned WEAKENS, whose pre-stated consequence was a kidney-led framing; WEAKENS stands at its first-round value (Section S-R9). Measured-protein-scaled comparison of the two previously reported signals: no detectable difference in arginine per SD of ARG1 (the marginal, covariance-aware estimate with second-order SE on the 503 panel), an interval that does not establish equivalence because it does not exclude differences from −31% to 54%; ornithine did not scale in the same proportion, but its association at signal A did not colocalize with the protein (PP.H4 0.34 on the 503 panel and 0.26 on the 489 panel), so that ratio is not tied to the protein signal, and the contrast is a supported statistical contrast, not proof that ARG1 produces different biological effects at the two signals; T2D differed at nominal significance on the pre-declared conditional estimate in FinnGen (p 0.037; Holm-adjusted p 0.22, so nominal rather than multiplicity-robust) and on the pre-declared marginal estimate in DIAMANTE (p 0.026)
full_main_uncertainty: No divergence claim: a direct comparison of T2D with arginine across the signals did not establish that they scale differently (in FinnGen p 0.046 conditional and 0.062 marginal; in DIAMANTE both p values were below 0.05, so these tests are not uniformly negative), the requirement for a divergence claim, p < 0.05 under both estimands in FinnGen, was not met and was set after both p values were seen, and the results establish neither a null at signal B nor the absence of an ARG1-mediated mechanism. The T2D contrast is sensitive to the reference LD in FinnGen (bootstrap share 0.84 against a 0.90 rule), as is the FinnGen conditional direct comparison (0.62), the sign of the correlation between the signals is not identified, and DIAMANTE, which may share participants with FinnGen, is not independent confirmation. Reference-LD fit inadmissible (s 0.148). The gene behind signal A's T2D association is unresolved, and the East Asian instrument does not test signal A
full_next_biological_question: Do the two signals differ for T2D in a large resource not used to select the locus, with adequate representation of the signal-B allele, and do arginase activity and ARG1 abundance, measured by genotype at each signal, track the difference?

Reported before: plasma FGFR4 linked to T2D at this locus [@new:Koprulu2023FGFR4] and in an East Asian phenome-wide MR study [@new:LiuX2025FGFR4]. In clinical development: roblitinib (FGF401), an FGFR4-selective inhibitor, in oncology; agrees only if the instrument tracks abundance. Aldafermin, an FGFR4–β-klotho activator, acts the opposite way
adds: CKB instrument, AGEN: higher FGFR4 with higher risk, p = 3.9 × 10⁻¹²; PP.H4 0.989 (0.897 conservative). TPMI: discovery sign, p = 0.0012; concordant, Bonferroni; corroborated in an external East Asian check
main_uncertainty: Instrument in LD with Gly388Arg (r² 0.97). Gly388Arg lies in the transmembrane domain; effects on receptor abundance or function and assay-related effects remain unresolved. Whether the measured plasma form contains this residue is unknown. Whether AGEN and TPMI share participants was not checked; European p = 0.27, a non-rejection
next_biological_question: Is the association carried by FGFR4 abundance, measured with an assay insensitive to Gly388Arg, by the variant's effect on the receptor, or by both, tested in further East Asian T2D cohorts?

discovery_basis: UMOD-eGFR (multi-signal candidate): discovery Wald ratio on the eGFR* scale (-ln(eGFR) per SD of protein; positive = lower eGFR)
literature_status: Reported before: risk alleles raise uromodulin and damage the kidney [@new:Trudu2013UMOD]; blood uromodulin and CKD by MR [@new:Sjaarda2018UMOD]
search_scope: PubMed: (UMOD OR uromodulin) AND "Mendelian randomization" AND ("glomerular filtration rate" OR "kidney function" OR "chronic kidney disease") (hits 11, screened 11)
established_role_reported_before: Role: made only in the kidney, by epithelial cells of the thick ascending limb and distal convoluted tubule; the most abundant protein in normal urine [@new:UniProt2025]. Reported before: risk alleles raise uromodulin and damage the kidney [@new:Trudu2013UMOD]; blood uromodulin and CKD by MR [@new:Sjaarda2018UMOD]. Tractable (antibody), no agent in the clinic
adds: Control for the signal-level tests: both declared signals colocalized with eGFR (PP.H4 0.97 and 1.00 on the 503 panel), and no heterogeneity was detected in eGFR per SD of UMOD across its five protein signals (p 0.45)
main_uncertainty: One worked control: the non-rejection does not show proportionality. Reference-LD fine-mapping inadmissible (s 0.297) and not cited as support; the colocalization values are conditional coloc.abf results. No external outcome check
next_biological_question: Does plasma uromodulin reflect renal production at each signal, tested by multi-signal colocalization with in-sample LD in an independent Olink cohort?
full_established_role_reported_before: Role: made only in the kidney, by epithelial cells of the thick ascending limb and distal convoluted tubule; the most abundant protein in normal urine [@new:UniProt2025]. Reported before: risk alleles raise uromodulin and damage the kidney [@new:Trudu2013UMOD]; blood uromodulin and CKD by MR [@new:Sjaarda2018UMOD]. Tractable (antibody), no agent in the clinic
full_adds: Control for the signal-level tests: both declared signals colocalized with eGFR (PP.H4 0.97 and 1.00 on the 503 panel; 0.97 and 1.00 on its 489 subset), and no heterogeneity was detected in eGFR per SD of UMOD across its five protein signals (p 0.45)
full_main_uncertainty: One worked control: the non-rejection does not show proportionality, and a palindromic signal sits inside the test (without it, p 0.364). Reference-LD fine-mapping inadmissible (s 0.297) and not cited as support. The colocalization values are conditional coloc.abf results, not a fine-mapping fit, and were checked only for agreement between the two panels, a necessary check and not independent confirmation because the 489 panel is a 97% nested subset; the conditioning used one variant set per panel (protein s 0.280 on the 503 panel and 0.285 on the 489 panel). Robustness to the reference LD was evaluated only on the all-signal test. No external outcome check
full_next_biological_question: Does plasma uromodulin reflect renal production at each signal, tested by multi-signal colocalization with in-sample LD in an independent Olink cohort?

table_row_label: DPEP1–eGFR, with cysteinylglycine; multi-signal candidate, not graded
discovery_basis: DPEP1-eGFR (multi-signal candidate): discovery Wald ratio on the eGFR* scale (-ln(eGFR) per SD of protein; positive = lower eGFR)
literature_status: Reported before: the *DPEP1*–*CHMP1A* kidney-function locus, both genes causal in mice [@new:Guan2021DPEP1]
search_scope: PubMed: (DPEP1 OR "dipeptidase 1" OR "renal dipeptidase") AND "Mendelian randomization" (hits 5, screened 5)
established_role_reported_before: Role: dipeptidase that hydrolyzes dipeptides, including cystinyl-bis-glycine formed during glutathione degradation [@new:UniProt2025]; renal dipeptidase hydrolyzes cysteinylglycine [@old:29]. Reported before: the *DPEP1*–*CHMP1A* kidney-function locus, both genes causal in mice [@new:Guan2021DPEP1]. Approved: cilastatin inhibits DPEP1, agreeing with the eGFR direction and opposing the DPEP1–AF direction (Additional file 1: Table S4)
adds: Cysteinylglycine colocalized under the single-causal-variant model (coloc.abf, PP.H4 0.998). Across five protein signals, no detectable difference in cysteinylglycine (p 0.98) or eGFR (p 0.11) per SD of DPEP1; on the declared secondary set of signals, eGFR differed (p 0.025)
main_uncertainty: Reference-LD fine-mapping inadmissible and not cited as support; attribution between *DPEP1* and *CHMP1A* unresolved; no external outcome check. For eGFR, the protein's conditional PP.H4 is below the colocalization threshold at all five signals, so the comparison is not tied to colocalized signals
next_biological_question: Do cysteinylglycine and eGFR differ by Glu351Gln genotype, with in-sample LD in an independent Olink cohort?
